ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Extremely low macro-level ratio; the visible surface consists of approximately 98% low-intensity (black) pixels with <2% high-intensity (white) pixels localized to discrete spots.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: Solid low-intensity (black) pigmentation across the entire visible surface; no contiguous white geometric blobs, mottling, or banding patterns are present.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep, acute-angled V-shaped central depression with a sharp vertex; the bounding-box depth is approximately 25% of the vertical extent of the visible fluke lobes.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: Continuous non-linear boundary; the left lobe trailing edge features approximately 8-10 broad, rounded scalloped peaks; the right lobe features a higher frequency of lower-amplitude micro-serrations.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Left lobe follows a broad convex arc terminating in a rounded distal tip; right lobe exhibits an elongated, tapered trajectory ending in a sharply pointed distal tip.

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Localized clusters of small, circular high-contrast white pixels are detected along the left distal margin, the central proximal base area, and the extreme distal tip of the right lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Visible accumulation of high-contrast white material and irregular, bulbous surface topography on the distal margin of the left lobe, indicating significant barnacle colonization.
other_distinctive_markers: Uniform dark pigmentation across the entire visible ventral surface, characteristic of an all-black (Type 5) humpback whale fluke phenotype.
